messages:
jordan: Hey team — escalating a customer case where SSE stream consistently drops the final chunk after a client reconnect. Customer sees partial JSON (missing final `finish_reason`) and no trailing event. Happens only when their Windows client reconnects quickly (~300ms).

maria: Thanks — can you paste minimal repro + headers? Is this specific to our hosted endpoint or repros on dedicated/private too?

jordan: Hosted. Repro steps from customer (condensed):
1) start stream via chunked SSE: `GET /v1/streams?model=rw-7b`
2) read 95% tokens, then force a reconnect (simulate network blip) by closing socket, re-open within 250-350ms, resume using `Last-Event-ID` resume header
3) client receives everything except the final event with `{"finish_reason":"stop"}`. JSON ends with trailing partial chunk like `..."token":"...` and then socket close.

Logs they provided:
```
[client] recv: data: {"id":"tok_123","data":{"delta":"..."}}
[client] reconnect after 310ms with Last-Event-ID: tok_123
[client] recv: data: {"id":"tok_124","data":{"delta":"..."}}
[client] recv: data: {"id":"tok_125","data":{"delta":"\"incomplete"}}
[client] connection closed by remote
```

They tried increasing backoff to 1s and the final chunk arrives 100% of the time. So seems timing sensitive.

samir: Hmm — sounds like a race where our connection rejoin path is not flushing final buffered event for quick reconnects. Any proxy/edge in front of customer? They mentioned corporate firewall + Cloudflare.

jordan: Customer traffic goes through Cloudflare (managed) -> our ELB -> Fastly -> edge pool -> runtime. They reproduced hitting edge pool directly (bypassing CF) and still saw the issue.

maria: Can you capture the server side trace for the thread id or request id? If we see the last SSE frame emitted by the runtime but not delivered, it narrows down. Also, do we set `Connection: keep-alive` and chunking headers correctly on resume?

jordan: Attached request-id: req_0a7c (from client). They also captured tcpdump showing server sent final 2 packets with `finish_reason` then immediate FIN from Fastly side. Snippet: `... "finish_reason":"stop"}\r\n\r\n` then `RST` a few ms later.

ken: That RST is interesting. If the intermediate closes before client reads tail, client will see truncate. Fastly or our edge might be sending RST when connection re-associated. Could be a winsock/tcp-timers interaction on Windows client causing it to miss last bytes if the server side connection is torn down quickly.

maria: Agreed. Two action items: 1) infra capture of edge/fastly logs for req_0a7c with timestamps around 1739004321.*; 2) runtime team to verify that on resume/fallback we flush any buffered final event and delay connection close by 500ms (configurable) to tolerate quick client reconnects.

samir: I'll pull edge logs now (cc @support-bot to auto-attach flow logs).

support-bot: Attached: fastly-edge-log-req_0a7c.gz (s3://redwood-support/attachments/fastly/req_0a7c.gz) — shows final SSE event outbound at 2024-06-12T15:12:05.312Z, FIN at 2024-06-12T15:12:05.318Z.

jordan: Customer confirmed they reconnected at 2024-06-12T15:12:05.320Z (client clock within 10ms). So rejoin was ~2ms after FIN.

maria: If Fastly is closing connection (FIN) and client reopens before TCP stack drains, client-side socket might get EOF and lose trailing bytes. Two mitigations: 1) Ensure edge delays FIN until ACK from client or after small grace period (250-500ms) when resuming; 2) On runtime side, add a terminal heartbeat SSE event `event: terminal` with base64 checksum so clients can detect incomplete terminal events.

ken: For urgent workaround, recommend customer increase reconnect backoff to >=500ms. Also we can enable `resume_strict=false` for them so server will send a short `resume_marker` event frequently which helps detect truncation.

jordan: Customer wants P1 fix because it breaks production UIs. Can we root cause quickly?

maria: I'll open a runtime PR to add a 300ms configurable drain window before closing the final connection and add extra flush on rejoin. Samir, can you confirm if Fastly can be tuned to hold FIN for short window?

samir: Will check with edge infra/fastly config. If Fastly is proxying and sees backend FIN, it might close to client immediately. We can insert delay via `graceful_close_ms` flag on proxy layer. I'll test on a canary.

jordan: Thanks. I'll tell the customer the workaround (backoff >=500ms) and that we have an internal canary to try. They asked for reproducible curl incantation — here's one that reproduces when run on Windows + netcat disconnect: 
```
curl -s -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=rw-7b" | awk '/data:/ {print $0} NR%200==0{system("sleep 0.3; kill -INT $(pgrep -f curl) || true")}'
```

jordan: Will update thread with edge logs + runtime PR link. Please @maria @samir confirm when canary rolled out and I'll mark customer update. :pray:

maria: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime/pull/987 — adds 300ms drain + flush on resume. Will monitor canary metrics.

samir: Fastly flag toggled in staging; canary shows no client-facing truncations on repeated reconnects. Rolling to prod tomorrow morning.

jordan: Great — customer notified. Closing escalation when prod roll passes. Thanks all :heart:
